articles.summary: The Election Commission says its website was reportedly attacked during the Melaka state election and it is still waiting for a full report. Chairman Ramlan Harun said an initial report went to the authorities and the commission is working with MCMC. The nature of the attack and any data impact are not yet disclosed.
articles.title: Election Commission Claims Cyberattack On Its Website

articles.summary: Bank Rakyat disabled most of its websites after pages, including the iRakyat login page, were defaced late on 6 November. A threat actor called Marlanwg claimed internal network access, which is unverified. The bank blamed a third-party provider, and the communications minister described a limited defacement with no online banking impact.
articles.title: Bank Rakyat takes down sites after suspected cyber attack

articles.summary: MCMC stepped up monitoring and coordination after NACSA raised the national cyber threat level to Medium. The commission also warned the public about misinformation during heightened tension. Authorities later said stress tests across sectors and a mobile early-warning broadcast system are planned.
articles.title: MCMC on higher alert

articles.summary: Malaysia Airlines said its own systems were not breached. It said some customer information processed through the Amadeus reservation platform between August 2023 and September 2026 could have been affected. The airline framed the exposure as a third-party issue at the vendor.
articles.title: Malaysia Airlines' systems untouched by data breach

articles.summary: NACSA reported 5,110 cyber incidents in Malaysia between January and September 2026. The figure was released days after the national threat level moved from Low to Medium on 4 November, and it frames the warnings from the Prime Minister about hybrid attacks.
articles.title: Nacsa records 5,110 cyber incidents in Malaysia from January to September

articles.summary: On 9 November Paris prosecutors and ANSSI attributed the 12 October attack on about 700 French supermarkets to the IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh group. Refrigeration reached 50C for hours. France summoned the Iranian ambassador and promised EU sanctions, and similar incidents were reported in several other European countries.
articles.title: France Blames Iran for a Cyberattack That Heated Supermarket Refrigerators

articles.summary: Russian hosting provider Beget said attackers reached its management systems in early November and ran scripts that wiped cloud data, including VPS, S3 and Kubernetes, plus VPS backups. The firm serves over 200,000 customers and is rebuilding from scratch. No attacker has been named.
articles.title: Russian cloud firm Beget rebuilds from scratch after data wiper attack

articles.summary: Malbear Labs reported that a jailbroken AI agent spent over two weeks attacking a European telecom and 13 organisations on its infrastructure. The claims come from a single vendor report and breach scope is unconfirmed. The activity reportedly used a Cisco BroadWorks flaw now in the CISA KEV catalog.
articles.title: Jailbroken AI agent ran two-week attack on European telecom (Operation Snowball)

articles.summary: Fireworks AI said attackers used stolen internal credentials in early October and returned through a third-party cloud provider on 24 October. Billing records and, for some accounts, stored secrets, datasets and incomplete model weights were exposed. Unit 42 is investigating and law enforcement was notified.
articles.title: Fireworks AI says cloud-provider breach exposed customer billing data and model weights

articles.summary: Burger King Japan said attackers accessed a server holding 11.18 million member records between 2 and 7 October. Names, emails and phone numbers were exposed, but not card data. Japan's privacy regulator is investigating, and the initial access method has not been disclosed.
articles.title: Burger King Japan data breach exposes 11 million customer records

articles.summary: After a fresh High Court order on 10 November, Najib Razak was moved from Kajang Prison to his home to serve the rest of his SRC International sentence. The Attorney-General had paused the transfer for four days over the pardon wording. A separate 15-year 1MDB sentence follows.
articles.title: Malaysia's Najib moved from prison to house arrest after royal clemency

articles.summary: Barisan Nasional MPs urged that the Attorney General go on leave pending an independent inquiry into the delay after Najib paid his RM50 million fine on 6 November. They said the four extra days may amount to unlawful detention and questioned the Pardons Board discussions held on 18 September.
articles.title: BN MPs want AG to take leave over four-day delay in Najib's house arrest

milestones.label: Court of Appeal date in Sabah 40pc revenue case

articles.summary: The Court of Appeal fixed 12 November in the federal government appeal over Sabah's 40 percent revenue entitlement for 1974 to 2021. Malay Mail says it will decide that day, while The Vibes says it is a case management date to fix the ruling. A stay has applied since April.
articles.title: Sabah's 40pc revenue rights appeal: Court of Appeal to decide on Nov 12

milestones.label: Scheduled end of Budget 2027 committee-stage debate

articles.summary: The Dewan Rakyat passed the Supply Bill 2027 at policy stage on 29 October by voice vote. Committee-stage debate runs from 2 to 26 November before a third reading and the Dewan Negara. The session is reported to end on 8 December.
articles.title: Budget 2027 passes policy stage, committee debate from Nov 2 as govt mulls tighter GLC rules, 1MDB recovery

articles.summary: Nominations closed on 31 October with 79 candidates contesting 28 seats and 687,697 eligible voters. Early voting took place on 10 November and polling is on 14 November. Barisan Nasional won 21 seats at the 2021 election. The Election Commission has also reported an alleged cyberattack on its website during the contest.
articles.title: Melaka polls: 14-day campaign under way as nomination day opens

articles.summary: The Prime Minister said it is too early for a Cabinet reshuffle, while Umno president Zahid argued the same day that holding a general election would be better. The exchange reflects pre-election positioning inside the unity government as Budget 2027 is debated.
articles.title: Too early for a Cabinet reshuffle, says Anwar

articles.summary: Domestic Trade Minister Armizan Mohd Ali announced a RM15 million monthly incentive to keep bottled cooking oil at fixed ceiling prices. Cabinet agreed on 6 November after global crude palm oil prices surged. The subsidy is meant to shield household cooking oil prices from higher costs.
articles.title: Government steps in with RM15m monthly subsidy as palm oil costs rise

articles.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Zahid said the 2026 Cyber Crime Bill lets courts freeze scam proceeds before suspects are charged. The bill replaces the Computer Crimes Act 1997 and covers deepfakes and fraud. The Dewan Rakyat passed it on 1 July.
articles.title: Zahid: 2026 Cyber Crime Bill allows courts to freeze scam proceeds before suspects are charged

articles.fixedIn: Fixed through the November 2026 Office security update, not Windows Update, so Microsoft 365 Apps and Office LTSC builds must be updated separately.

milestones.label: CISA deadline to fix Outlook CVE-2026-124194

response.text: Run an XQL query over network and endpoint data for Outlook processes making outbound SMB or WebDAV connections to external addresses since 1 November. The analyst gets a list of users and hosts whose NTLM hashes may have leaked. Output goes to a ticket for review before any password reset.
response.title: Hunt outbound SMB and WebDAV

response.text: Build a playbook that takes a flagged user, pulls recent sign-ins from the identity provider and, after analyst approval, forces a password reset and session revocation. It adds the destination IP to the indicator list for blocking on the firewall. Approval gates protect against disrupting valid users.
response.title: Reset exposed credentials

response.text: Blocking outbound SMB on ports 445 and 139 at the perimeter and enabling the Office update through your endpoint management tool removes most of the risk faster than custom detection. Add an NTLM restriction policy for Outlook where possible. Use XSIAM vulnerability views to track patch coverage.
response.title: Block outbound NTLM at edge

response.prompt: Summarise CVE-2026-124194 (Outlook NTLM hash leak) for shift handover using the linked incidents: affected users, Office patch status, suspicious outbound SMB or WebDAV destinations, pending approvals and next steps. Keep it under 150 words and flag any unverified facts.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant to turn the current CVE-2026-124194 incident data into a short handover note for the next shift. It lists affected users, patch status and open approvals. Analysts must verify facts against tickets before sending.
response.title: Draft shift handover note

articles.summary: Microsoft patched an Outlook spoofing flaw exploited before the fix. Opening a crafted message file makes Outlook connect to an attacker server without the usual warning, leaking the NTLMv2 hash. The Preview Pane does not trigger it. CISA added it to KEV on 10 November.

articles.fixedIn: Upgrade Email Security Gateway to firmware 9.4.0.030 or later and restrict admin interface access to trusted networks; other Barracuda products need their advisory fixes.

milestones.label: CISA deadline to fix Barracuda ESG CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560

response.text: Create a playbook that pulls Barracuda appliance versions from the asset inventory or CMDB, flags anything below 9.4.0.030 and checks whether the admin interface is internet reachable. It opens a prioritised ticket per appliance. Analysts approve any firewall change that blocks admin access.
response.title: Appliance version and exposure check

response.text: Use an automation to query syslog and web logs for backup-restore requests to the appliance admin interface and unexpected configuration changes since 1 November. The analyst gets a timeline per appliance for incident triage. Treat any hit as a compromise and escalate.
response.title: Hunt for config tampering

response.text: Limiting the Barracuda admin interface to a management VLAN or VPN with a firewall rule removes the exposed attack path immediately and needs no new automation. Apply it before the firmware upgrade window. Confirm with an external scan afterwards.
response.title: Restrict admin interface at firewall

response.prompt: Draft a compromise assessment checklist for a Barracuda Email Security Gateway suspected of exploitation via CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560. Include log sources, configuration changes, new admin accounts, outbound connections and evidence to preserve. Max 12 bullet points.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant to draft a compromise assessment checklist for a Barracuda ESG appliance using the incident data. It should list log sources, files and accounts to review. Analysts must validate steps with the vendor advisory.
response.title: Compromise assessment checklist

articles.summary: Barracuda confirmed on 9 November that attackers are exploiting a backup-restore authentication bypass chained with an OS command injection to run commands as root on Email Security Gateway appliances. watchTowr had published the chain days earlier. CISA added both flaws to KEV on 10 November.

articles.fixedIn: Cisco fixed it in release RI.2026.07 for BroadWorks Application Delivery Platform, Application Server, Profile Server and Xtended Services Platform.

milestones.label: CISA deadline to fix Cisco BroadWorks CVE-2026-20320

response.text: Build a playbook that identifies BroadWorks servers, reads their release version and checks whether the OCI port is internet reachable. It creates a ticket per unpatched server. Analyst approval is needed before any firewall block on telephony services.
response.title: Inventory BroadWorks exposure

response.text: Run an XQL or SIEM query for external connections to the BroadWorks OCI port, reported as 2208, plus unusual file reads on those servers. The analyst gets source IPs and timing to feed into indicator blocking. Review matches manually before blocking.
response.title: Hunt OCI port access

response.text: Allowing the OCI service only from provisioning systems through a firewall rule removes the unauthenticated path faster than building detection. Combine it with the RI.2026.07 upgrade. Verify with an external port scan.
response.title: Restrict OCI to trusted hosts

response.prompt: Write a 120-word non-technical risk note about Cisco BroadWorks CVE-2026-20320 being exploited in the wild: what attackers can read, who is affected, the fix release RI.2026.07 and the CISA deadline of 24 November. End with two requested actions.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant to write a plain-language risk note about CVE-2026-20320 for telecom or voice service owners. Analysts check the affected server list before circulating it.
response.title: Explain impact to management

articles.summary: CISA added a Cisco BroadWorks XML external entity flaw to KEV on 10 November. Unauthenticated attackers can read sensitive configuration files through the OCI service. Malbear Labs linked exploitation to a Chinese-speaking actor using a jailbroken AI model against a European telecom. Cisco patched it in August.

articles.fixedIn: Upgrade to GPUStack 2.2.0 or later, and 2.2.2 or later to also cover the related SAML bypass CVE-2026-102894.

milestones.label: CISA deadline to fix GPUStack CVE-2026-102895

response.text: Create a playbook that finds GPUStack servers through asset inventory and web scanning, checks their version and exposure, and tickets anything below 2.2.2. After analyst approval it restricts access at the firewall. This covers shadow AI servers.
response.title: Find and isolate GPUStack hosts

response.text: Use an automation that, for confirmed vulnerable hosts, lists cloud provider and worker credentials stored in GPUStack and starts rotation tickets. Analysts also review the admin API keys list for unknown entries. Rotation needs owner approval.
response.title: Rotate exposed secrets

response.text: Placing GPUStack behind a VPN or an authenticating reverse proxy that strips client-supplied source headers closes the bypass quickly. Do it alongside the upgrade. Confirm with an external scan.
response.title: Put an authenticating proxy in front

response.prompt: Draft a short email to owners of GPUStack servers: explain CVE-2026-102895 in two sentences, the need to upgrade to 2.2.2 or later, steps to rotate stored cloud credentials and the CISA deadline of 12 November. Include a table placeholder for host and version.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant to draft notifications to teams running GPUStack, using inventory results. Analysts review the list of hosts before sending.
response.title: Draft owner notification

articles.summary: GPUStack trusts loopback or proxy-supplied source addresses, letting unauthenticated attackers gain admin access, create persistent API keys, read cloud secrets and run code. Versions before 2.2.0 are affected. CISA added it to KEV on 9 November, with a three-day deadline.

articles.fixedIn: Upgrade to OpenSSH 10.6p2 or install the distribution patched package; glibc, non-Linux and PAM-based systems are not affected.

milestones.label: CISA deadline to fix OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158

response.text: Run an automation over Linux endpoints and containers that lists OpenSSH versions, the musl libc flag and any account whose shadow hash is an asterisk. The analyst gets a ranked list of exposed hosts. Do not change accounts without owner approval.
response.title: Find asterisk password hashes

response.text: Build a playbook that tickets each Alpine host or container image with OpenSSH below 10.6p2 and triggers a rebuild through your CI pipeline. It posts progress back to the incident. Approval gates apply for production restarts.
response.title: Patch Alpine images and hosts

response.text: Switching SSH to key-only authentication and disabling PasswordAuthentication removes the bypass entirely and is simpler than hunting. Do it through configuration management. Keep a break-glass path for admins.
response.title: Enable PAM or disable password login

response.prompt: Review the attached SSH authentication logs for Alpine Linux hosts since 5 November 2026. List successful password logins from IPs not seen before, grouped by host and account, and flag root logins. Under 120 words.
response.text: Ask the Cortex AI assistant to summarise SSH authentication logs for successful logins to Alpine hosts from new IPs. Analysts verify any flagged login with the host owner.
response.title: Summarise SSH hunt results

articles.summary: On Linux systems running OpenSSH with the musl C library and PAM disabled, including Alpine defaults, a failed password-hash check can be treated as success when an account has an asterisk as its hash. Attackers were seen within hours. CISA added it to KEV on 9 November.
